title: From Soil to Software: Experience from a STEM Workshop on Smart Plant Care and Teachable Machines
problem: Traditional STEM education lacks hands-on, integrated experience with data acquisition, machine learning, and AI. High school students need practical engagement with real-world computing applications.
method: STEM workshop (3 days, Toledo EXCEL program) combining custom-built IoT sensor system with MakeCode visual programming and Teachable Machine for ML. Students created smart plant care assistant and trained ML classifiers.

title: 17.1: Sensor-Less Laser Voltage-Probing Attack Detection via Run-Time-Leakage-Shift Monitoring with 4.35% Area Overhead
problem: Laser voltage probing (LVP) attacks on integrated circuits achieve near-100% success rate by probing on-chip voltages through backside laser illumination with high spatial resolution and low cost. Current detection approaches lack effective sensor-less mechanisms to counter these physical attacks in cost-constrained systems.
method: The design uses run-time leakage-shift monitoring to detect laser-induced anomalies without dedicated attack sensors. By observing shifts in device leakage currents caused by photocurrent injection during LVP attacks, the circuit can trigger countermeasures with minimal area overhead (4.35%).

title: Network Replay and Consistency Across Testbeds
problem: Shared network testbeds introduce variability (jitter, loss) that degrades experiment fidelity and reproducibility; difficult to quantify testbed quality.
method: Choir: 100 Gbps network replay tool running on commodity hardware with novel consistency metric for cross-testbed comparison.

title: RISC-V Based Secure Processor Architecture for Return Address Protection
problem: RISC-V embedded systems vulnerable to buffer overflow attacks, particularly stack-based attacks that alter program control flow. Memory-based attacks are significant challenge for RISC-V security.
method: Hardware-based approach leveraging existing Return Address Stack (RAS) with minimal microarchitecture changes and limited software overhead. Protects against buffer overflow attacks targeting control flow. Tested with buffer-intensive benchmarks and RIPE benchmark.

title: ReMaP: Macro Placement by Recursively Prototyping and Periphery-Guided Relocating
problem: Macro placement in chip floorplanning directly impacts timing (WNS/TNS) and dataflow efficiency, but expert-quality placement is time-consuming to generate. Existing macro placers lack structured approaches to place macros near periphery while optimizing dataflow and avoiding overlaps.
method: ReMaP uses a two-phase approach: ABPlace (angle-based analytical method) arranges macros along an ellipse capturing both dataflow optimization and overlap avoidance, producing rough periphery-aligned distributions. Follow-up heuristic positions macros along chip boundaries, mimicking expert practice. Recursive refinement improves placement quality iteratively. Parameter autotuning via search optimizes tool knobs.

title: Faster Chaitin-like Register Allocation via Grammatical Decompositions of Control-Flow Graphs
problem: Register allocation via graph coloring (Chaitin-style) is NP-hard in general, but practical compilers rely on heuristics that do not exploit the sparse, structured nature of real program control-flow graphs (CFGs). This leads to suboptimal allocation or unnecessary spills in programs with structured control flow.
method: The paper formalizes the sparsity of structured program CFGs using graph-theoretic parameters (treewidth, pathwidth) and introduces a grammatical decomposition—parsing the CFG into a tree decomposition. Register allocation is then solved efficiently via dynamic programming on this tree decomposition, yielding a parameterized algorithm whose complexity scales with the treewidth of the CFG rather than graph size alone. This exploits the observation that real programs' CFGs have small treewidth, making previously intractable exact or near-exact coloring feasible.

title: 14.6 A 28nm 64kb Bit-Rotated Hybrid-CIM Macro with an Embedded Sign-Bit-Processing Array and a Multi-Bit-Fusion Dual-Granularity Cooperative Quantizer
problem: Hybrid compute-in-memory (HCIM) designs face three key challenges: (1) optimally defining the digital-analog boundary without sacrificing accuracy or overhead, (2) handling sign-bit processing overhead in bit-rotated schemes, and (3) wasting energy on low-accuracy-contributed low-bit quantization in analog portions.
method: A 64 kb hybrid CIM macro using bit-rotated feature-in scheme that considers sign-bits in the first product-wise adder, eliminating error-pollution problems from bit-parallel/serial approaches. An embedded sign-bit-processing array handles signed-unsigned compression. A multi-bit-fusion dual-granularity cooperative quantizer dynamically allocates precision between analog and digital portions based on bit-significance.

title: Fast On-device LLM Inference with NPUs
problem: On-device LLM inference on mobile NPUs incurs unacceptably high latency, particularly during the prefill stage, because existing NPU programming models are not designed to efficiently map the irregular, attention-heavy computation patterns of LLMs. Even mobile-sized models (e.g., Gemma-2B) run too slowly for interactive tasks such as screen UI understanding.
method: The system analyzes the NPU execution bottlenecks of mobile LLMs and redesigns the inference pipeline to exploit NPU-specific parallelism. It introduces operator fusion and tiling strategies tailored to NPU dataflow constraints, and reorders computation to overlap NPU and CPU execution. The approach targets the prefill stage specifically, batching token processing to amortize NPU invocation overhead and restructuring attention kernels to fit the NPU's fixed-function units.

title: Adaptive CHERI Compartmentalization for Heterogeneous Accelerators
problem: Hardware accelerators in heterogeneous systems lack fine-grained memory protection: IOMMU-based isolation operates at page granularity, leaving intra-page accesses unprotected, while per-accelerator memory safety modifications require significant engineering effort and do not scale across diverse accelerator types.
method: CapChecker is an adaptive hardware interface inserted between CHERI-unaware accelerators and the system memory bus. It imports capability metadata from the CPU's CHERI register file and enforces pointer-level bounds and permission checks on every memory access issued by the accelerator, without modifying the accelerator architecture itself. The interface interposes on the accelerator's memory request channel, decodes the capability tag and bounds from the CPU-managed capability table, and raises a fault on any out-of-bounds or permission-violating access. Capability grants from the CPU are communicated through a lightweight descriptor mechanism that maps accelerator DMA addresses to CHERI capabilities.

title: Redesigning GROMACS Halo Exchange: Improving Strong Scaling with GPU-initiated NVSHMEM
problem: GROMACS molecular dynamics simulations achieve strong scaling poorly on heterogeneous supercomputers. MPI's CPU-centric communication introduces latencies that hinder GPU utilization and scalability on latency-sensitive (sub-millisecond iteration) workloads.
method: NVSHMEM-based GPU kernel-initiated redesign of domain decomposition halo-exchange. Fuses data packing and communication in GPU kernels. Leverages hardware latency-hiding (async copy engine over NVLink) for fine-grained overlap.

title: Drishti: Do Not Forget Slicing While Designing Last-Level Cache Replacement Policies for Many-Core Systems
problem: State-of-the-art LLC replacement policies (Hawkeye, Mockingjay) use a per-slice sampled cache and a per-slice reuse predictor that make myopic decisions based only on accesses to a single slice, unaware of global reuse behavior across all LLC slices in many-core systems; additionally, per-slice sampled cache sets receive insufficient LLC misses to drive accurate replacement decisions.
method: Drishti proposes two enhancements to existing LLC replacement policies for sliced LLCs: (1) a per-core global reuse predictor where each core's predictor is trained on all accesses by that core across all LLC slices—achieving global reuse awareness without centralized inter-slice interconnect traffic—combined with a local (per-slice) sampled cache that remains slice-local; (2) a per-slice dynamic sampled cache that adaptively expands the set of LLC sets used for sampling to improve the sample quality and ensure adequate miss coverage per slice. Evaluated by augmenting Hawkeye and Mockingjay on 4, 16, and 32-core systems with 8, 32, and 64 MB sliced LLCs.

title: DataMaestro: A Versatile and Efficient Data Streaming Engine Bringing Decoupled Memory Access To Dataflow Accelerators
problem: DNN inference on dataflow accelerators faces performance bottlenecks from data movement; accelerators lack decoupled access/execute architectures to mitigate memory access inefficiency and bank conflicts.
method: DataMaestro is a programmable data streaming unit supporting flexible access patterns, fine-grained prefetch and bank-conflict mitigation through dynamic addressing mode switching, and on-the-fly data manipulation to reduce memory footprints. Integrated with Tensor Core-like GeMM and quantization accelerators on RISC-V host with FPGA prototype and VLSI synthesis validation.

title: HPC Digital Twins for Evaluating Scheduling Policies, Incentive Structures and their Impact on Power and Cooling
problem: Evaluating scheduler policies and their physical infrastructure impact is limited to post-deployment analysis or simulators that don't model infrastructure. Need way to evaluate scheduler impact on power, cooling, and sustainability before deployment.
method: First digital twin framework extended with scheduling capabilities. Integrate datasets from top-tier HPC systems, implement extensions for external scheduling simulators. Implement incentive structures and ML-based scheduling evaluation.

title: A 212Gb/s PAM-4 Retimer with Integrated High-Swing Optical Driver and Chip-to-Module Long Reach Capability of 40dB in 5nm FinFET
problem: High-throughput AI/ML hyperscaler I/O interfaces require 200Gb/s+ per lane with low power budget; chip-to-module (C2M) electrical interconnects have high channel loss (~40dB) requiring equalization; eliminating external laser drivers reduces cost and form factor.
method: A 4-lane 212.5Gb/s/lane PAM-4 retimer integrates high-swing laser driver directly on the TX line driver, implements 40dB C2M channel equalization via receiver-side signal processing, and operates within power/thermal budgets for AI/ML workloads.

title: Late Breaking Results: A Fast Nearest Neighbor Search Acceleration for 3D Point Cloud
problem: K-Nearest Neighbors search in point clouds requires expensive Euclidean distance calculations over large candidate sets, limiting throughput on edge devices and real-time applications.
method: Uses locality-sensitive E2LSH partitioning to pre-filter candidate points, employs a precomparator module to reduce candidate search space further, and optimizes Euclidean distance computation to minimize expensive calculations while maintaining high precision.

title: Utilizing Sparsity in the GPU-accelerated Assembly of Schur Complement Matrices in Domain Decomposition Methods
problem: Domain decomposition methods compute Schur complement matrices for solving large engineering problems on HPC systems. GPU assembly of explicit dense Schur complements incurs significant overhead, adding overhead to GPU acceleration benefits.
method: GPU-accelerated Schur complement assembly exploiting matrix sparsity: (1) Direct GPU assembly avoiding host-side overhead, (2) Wisely utilize sparsity patterns to reduce memory and computation, (3) Applied to FETI (Finite Element Tearing and Interconnecting) method.
